findings.title: Two branches of getBaseConditions can never run
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object. Every path of `buildAuthorizationConditions` (lines 125-143) returns either a fragment or `NOTHING_CONDITION`, never null. So `authConditions` is always truthy, and the `else if (filterConditions)` branch (line 76) and the final `NOTHING_CONDITION` branch (line 79) can never run. They also suggest that filters alone could be applied without authorization, which is not the intent. A simpler version: `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${auth}) AND (${filterConditions})` : auth;`

findings.title: Constructor type no longer requires teamId for team scope
findings.body: The constructor used to take the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, so `scope: "team"` without `teamId` was a compile error. `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` makes `teamId` optional for every scope. A caller that leaves it out now compiles, fails `safeParse` at line 62, sets `options` to null, and gets `1=0`, an empty insights result with no error or log. If the looser type is needed for callers that hold a non-narrowed input, consider logging when validation fails, or keeping the union type and narrowing at the call site.

findings.title: Org/team `= ANY(array)` SQL never runs against the database
findings.body: The only test that runs the generated SQL (`getBaseConditions`, lines 480-484) uses `scope: "user"`. The org and team tests (lines 295-299, 332-343) only compare the `Prisma.Sql` objects structurally. So nothing checks that `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` and `"userId" = ANY(${ids})` bind correctly and return the right rows. That is exactly the part this rewrite from Prisma `in:` filters to raw SQL could break (array parameter typing, operator precedence of the OR/AND nesting). Consider adding a `$queryRaw` assertion for the org and team scopes, with one team booking and one personal booking each.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted while the caching code stays
findings.body: The `Caching` describe block was removed, but `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` still memoize into `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` (insightsBooking.ts:83-95). Those tests only needed their expected values changed to `Prisma.sql` form. Removing them leaves the memoization untested, including the `null`-vs-`undefined` distinction that keeps `getFilterConditions` from rebuilding when there are no filters.

contracts.action: Replace findMany (Prisma where-object query) with getBaseConditions returning a raw Prisma.Sql WHERE fragment
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed findMany, which ANDed authConditions and filterConditions into findManyArgs.where; sibling InsightsRoutingService builds the same org/team conditions as Prisma where-input objects
contracts.before_after: Before: auth and filter objects were ANDed; empty `userId in []` matched nothing. After: the same predicates as SQL fragments, each wrapped in parentheses when combined; an empty team user list leaves out the personal-booking clause, which matches the same rows as before
contracts.visible_effect: No production caller in the repository uses InsightsBookingService (a grep found only the test file), so nothing user-visible changes yet; callers must interpolate the fragment into $queryRaw themselves, as the test does
contracts.failure_mode: Invalid options or a non-admin user give `1=0`, so an empty result with no error. A team scope without teamId now type-checks and lands on this silent path (reported as a finding)

summary:
I found nothing that blocks the merge; all four findings are at "consider" severity. The rewrite of `InsightsBookingService` from Prisma where-objects to `Prisma.sql` fragments selects the same rows as before. Nothing outside the test file uses the service yet, so users won't see a change.

1. **Unreachable branches (`insightsBooking.ts:74`):** two branches in `getBaseConditions` can never run, because the authorization condition is always a SQL fragment, never null.
2. **Looser constructor type (`insightsBooking.ts:58`):** the new options type lets a team-scoped caller leave out `teamId` and still compile. That caller then gets an empty result (`1=0`) with no error or log.
3. **Untested org/team SQL (test file, line 481):** the only test that runs the generated SQL uses the user scope. The org and team `= ANY(array)` conditions are only compared as objects and never run against the database.
4. **Deleted caching tests (test file, line 435):** the caching tests were removed, but the caching code is still there and is now untested.
